author: Judahkerioth
quote:
The best: Everything. Special mention goes to the platforming and movement speed. There’s no shop or armor system, which really helps create a sense of urgency and survival. Boss fights: They're genuinely the protagonists of the story, not just random punching bags thrown in for the sake of having something to fight.What could be improved: Pretty much everything else.

Music: It's not Castlevania, but it does a good job.
Gameplay mechanics: Fun, addictive, and easy (it reminds me of Super Metroid).
Variety: Limited.
The bad: The card system is kind of... meh. It feels unnecessary. The Blasphemous-style relic system doesn't add much either. Basically, it's a +1 to damage in exchange for -2 health. Honestly, it's not worth ****'s a really good game, and I love that they're picking up the canon from this point onward. It gives them room to make the changes needed to modernize the series without losing what we love about it.

Combat: Dynamic, but with plenty of room for improvement. You have seven weapon types, and they're all really fun to use. However, each one eventually starts to feel repetitive (though that's not really a complaint. Every game eventually gets repetitive when it comes to combat).

Story: The best part of the game (especially if you're a fan of the series. If you're not, you'd probably be better off playing other Metroidvanias).

The really, really, REALLY bad: There's no extra game mode, such as Trevor Mode or The Creature Mode. This has been one of the series' iconic features ever since **** game has some mechanics that feel unnecessary, but I understand they're there as a tribute to the series' predecessors, while also incorporating more modern gameplay mechanics.
